cause.proximate_text: The cause of the elevated outboard bearing temperature was the maintenance procedure used for pump rebuild was not as detailed in accordance with the original manufacturer's recommendations for installation of the pump thrust bearing; specifically, the tightening of the thrust bearing locknut. The cause of the inboard bearing oil leak was a fabrication issue by the pump original manufacturer.
cause.theme: Two unrelated causes: maintenance procedure inadequacy (thrust bearing over-tightening) and original-manufacturer fabrication defect (labyrinth seal drain slot)

nodes.display_name: Thrust bearing locknut overtightened during rebuild
nodes.description: Maintenance procedure lacked detail per manufacturer recommendations, resulting in overtightening of the thrust bearing locknut during July 2022 pump replacement, adding excess pre-load to the bearing.
Excess pre-load combined with thrust load during operation caused further degradation of load-bearing surfaces and elevated bearing temperature.

nodes.display_name: Labyrinth seal drain slot improperly machined
nodes.description: Angled drain slot in inboard bearing cover was machined incorrectly due to a 2012 drawing update error, preventing the outer groove from draining back to the oil reservoir.
Improper drain slot configuration caused oil to leak from where the pump shaft protrudes through the inboard bearing cover.
